meta.title: Machine cross-checks of Kisumu values (independent second reading)
meta.rule: A machine reading by a different method from the original extraction. It is not editorial review: it never approves a value, it is shown on pages only as "machine cross-checked", and no record in data/reviews.json may cite it. Values where the check disagrees go to the top of docs/editorial/REVIEW_QUEUE.md.

methods.tesseract-600dpi-psm6: Page rendered at 600 dpi greyscale (pdftoppm) and read by tesseract 5, page segmentation mode 6, for values first read from the PDF text layer.
methods.tesseract-600dpi-psm4: Page rendered at 600 dpi greyscale and read by tesseract 5 in segmentation mode 4 (a different mode from the first OCR), for OCR values on pages with no text layer.
methods.pdf-text-layer: The PDF text layer of the page (pdftotext), for values first read by OCR.
methods.fallback: When the first second-method reading does not show the value, the page is read again by tesseract in the other segmentation mode (4 or 6) at 600 dpi.
methods.tesseract-300dpi-psm6: Further reading when the 600 dpi readings do not show the value: page rendered at 300 dpi (tesseract's training resolution) and read in segmentation mode 6; then mode 4, mode 1 (automatic orientation, for landscape tables), mode 11 (sparse text, for chart labels) and 200 dpi mode 6, stopping at the first that shows it. A method ending "+more" means none of the readings found it.
methods.parts: A stored total that the source prints only as its parts (recurrent and development pending bills; male and female counts; the Executive and Assembly payables tables) agrees when each part is found on the page by the same method and the parts add up to the stored value at its precision.

meta.match_rule: agree: the stored value appears among the numbers read on the page, in the stored unit or scaled to shillings, thousands, millions or billions, to the precision printed or to the precision stored, whichever is coarser (9223.35 KSh million agrees with a printed 9,223,350,139); numbers with fewer than three significant digits are not used, and a value printed only that way ("Kshs.2.4 billion") is not checkable.
